Dashboard: Recent Chats card (3 most-recent conversations + hotlinks)
## Goal

On the openthrottle-developer dashboard index (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/dashboard._index.tsx`), add a new card that lists the **3 most-recent agent conversations** ("chats") with per-chat hotlinks and a small footer of quick links to other useful spots.

## Context (verified in repo)

- The dashboard is a streamed grid: the loader returns two naked promises (`core`, `githubStats`) and each card renders inside `React.Suspense` + `Await`. New cards follow the same pattern.
- Conversations already have a server helper: `callListAgentConversations(request, { limit, offset, status })` in `app/global/utils/utils.agents-chat.ts`, backed by `ListAgentConversationsDocument` (already codegen'd — no new GraphQL needed).
- List-item shape `AgentConversationListItem` (from `@openthrottle/react-router-chat`): `{ id, status, title | null, updatedAt }`. Titles can be null → need a fallback label ("Untitled chat").
- The chat surface is the home route `/` (`app/routes/_index.tsx`). Opening a specific conversation is **client-only today** via `turn.restore({ conversationId })` — there is NO URL param to deep-link a chat. The `useConversationList` sidebar hook posts to `/resources/agent-conversations`.
- Existing "useful spots" links live in `WORKSPACE_FULL_JUMP_LINKS` (`~/routing/navigation/data/workspace-jump-links`), used by the (currently deprecated) `DashboardQuickNavigation`.

## Design decisions

1. **Data**: fetch the 3 most-recent conversations server-side in the dashboard loader via `callListAgentConversations(request, { limit: 3 })`, exposed as its own deferred promise (own `Await` boundary so it never blocks the activity chart, mirroring `githubStats`). Degrade gracefully via `errorElement` and an empty-state.
2. **Per-chat hotlink**: add a `?conversationId=<id>` deep-link so the card can link into a specific chat. Home `_index.tsx` reads the param on mount and calls `turn.restore({ conversationId })`. Card links to `/?conversationId=<id>`.
3. **Footer quick links**: "View all chats" (`/`), "New chat" (`/`), plus 2–3 curated useful spots reused from `WORKSPACE_FULL_JUMP_LINKS` (e.g. Plans, Queues, Pull Requests) — no bespoke link list.

## Conventions

- Generator-first: scaffold the component with `@tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component` (keep section comments, one component/file, props interface, copy in nearest `data/data.copy.ts`).
- shadcn primitives from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`; `Link` from `react-router`.
- Render-level Vitest tests (`component` not `screen`, `userEvent`). Show relative time for `updatedAt`.
- No codegen expected (reusing `ListAgentConversationsDocument`); if any GraphQL doc changes, run the codegen flow and commit `__generated__`.

## Out of scope

- Real-time updates of the card, pagination, rename/delete from the card.
Add a DashboardRecentChatsCard to the openthrottle-developer dashboard index that lists the 3 most-recent agent conversations and hotlinks to each chat plus a few useful destinations.

Reframe developer legal pages to Apache-2.0 open-core "steward" posture
## Goal

Update the posture and copy of the OpenThrottle Developer legal pages so they match the recent Apache-2.0 open-core relicense and read as a serious, invested product — while keeping the personal, solo-maker connection the owner values.

Scope is the three legal routes in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/` that are now stale:
- `legal.terms-of-use.tsx`
- `legal.privacy-policy.tsx`
- `legal._index.tsx`

`legal.license.tsx` was ALREADY updated to the Apache-2.0 open-core posture (open-core, Apache-2.0 core, reserved trademark, DCO sign-off) and is the reference voice to align the other three against. Do NOT rewrite the license page's substance; only touch it if a cross-link or a shared phrase needs to match.

## Why now

Two problems on the live pages:
1. **Direct contradiction** — `legal.terms-of-use.tsx` still says the source code is *"source-available and licensed under a proprietary End User License Agreement (EULA)"*, which conflicts with `legal.license.tsx` now declaring the core Apache-2.0. This must be fixed.
2. **Stale, self-deprecating posture** — terms-of-use, privacy-policy, and the legal index all open with *"a personal portfolio and developer playground … not a commercial product."* The owner wants these to read as a real, invested product without losing the personal connection.

## Locked decisions (owner-confirmed 2026-07-30)

- **Entity voice: "Steward + open project."** Frame OpenThrottle as an open-source product **stewarded by Matthew Scholta** — keep the solo-maker / personal-portfolio connection front-and-center and signal genuine investment, but drop the "just a playground / toy" framing. Not a company/"team" voice.
- **Keep ALL protective legal disclaimers.** Retain as-is / no-warranty / no-SLA / no-uptime-guarantee / limitation-of-liability language on terms-of-use (and the as-is note on privacy/index). Elevate the *tone*, not the legal protection. Do NOT soften disclaimers to "reasonable/best effort."

## Voice & terminology guardrails (apply to all three pages)

- Lead with OpenThrottle as an **open-source product** (open-core, Apache-2.0), **stewarded/built by Matthew Scholta**, rather than "a personal portfolio and developer playground."
- Keep the personal connection: Matthew Scholta is the named steward/author and the contact.
- Replace the EULA/"proprietary" framing in terms-of-use with the Apache-2.0 open-core framing, cross-linking to `/legal/license` (which already carries the full license explanation). Do not re-explain the whole license — defer to that page.
- Preserve the substance of every protective clause (acceptable use, disclaimer of warranties, limitation of liability, governing law, changes, contact). Only the framing/tone changes, plus the license correction.
- Keep using the shared constants (`SITE_TITLE`, `OPENTHROTTLE_CONTACT_PORTFOLIO`/`_REF`) and the existing `GlobalScreen`/`GlobalHeading` structure and section-comment scaffold — this is copy/posture work, not a component rewrite.

## Constraints

- Copy/JSX only; no new components, no schema/GraphQL changes, no new deps. Keep the generated section-comment scaffold (Hooks/Setup/Handlers/Markup/Life Cycle/🔌 Short Circuit).
- Validate with `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`; live-smoke the three routes in the dev server (`/legal`, `/legal/terms-of-use`, `/legal/privacy-policy`).
- Conventional commits; `Plan-Id:`/`Task-Id:` footers per task. Record the merged squash on the work ledger after merge.

## Out of scope

- The already-updated `legal.license.tsx` substance.
- Any legal pages in other apps (only `openthrottle-developer` has legal routes).
- Legal/attorney review — this is copy alignment, not legal sign-off.

Tool-agnostic git worktree setup (single entrypoint + self-heal)
Worktree setup (env reset, port remap, compose isolation, secret sync, install, build) currently only runs when a worktree is created through a tool-specific hook: Claude Code's `.claude/settings.json` WorktreeCreate hook (→ scripts/create_worktree.sh → scripts/setup_worktree.sh) or Cursor's `.cursor/worktrees.json` (→ scripts/setup_worktree.sh). A plain `git worktree add` (human at terminal, CI, another agent, a future editor) runs NOTHING — git has no native post-worktree-add hook. That gap produces stale/placeholder .env and login-type symptoms (e.g. the "default password too short" report).

Key finding: setup_worktree.sh does NOT seed the DB user/password, and neither does setup.sh. The default login user password (FullThrottle2026!) is set only by the separate, manual `pnpm database:bootstrap-default-user` (package.json:454). Worktrees deliberately SHARE the main checkout's Postgres/Redis, so the seeded user normally already exists — meaning the observed symptom is most likely an unconfigured worktree (.env never set up) or an unseeded shared DB, not something setup_worktree.sh would fix on its own.

Goal: make worktree provisioning "when we create a worktree we…" instead of "when Claude creates a worktree we…". Approach: (1) promote scripts/create_worktree.sh to a single tool-agnostic entrypoint that every consumer calls; (2) add an idempotent lazy self-heal guard on the dev entrypoint so any creation path is caught on first use; (3) resolve default-user seeding (guarded seed vs documented shared-DB dependency); (4) update docs. setup_worktree.sh is already idempotent, which makes the self-heal safe.

# Prune per-package OT projects

## Why
OT currently has a project for **every** workspace package (name starts with `@openthrottle/` or `@tools/`). That's 48 of the 61 total projects — far too granular. We keep the useful altitude: **one project per application** and **one per repo/workspace we bring in**. Package-level projects are noise and get deleted.

## Keep (13) — do NOT touch
- Apps: `OpenThrottle`, `OpenThrottle Admin`, `OpenThrottle CMS`, `OpenThrottle Developer`, `OpenThrottle Email`, `OpenThrottle Server`, `OpenThrottle Website`, `vscode-openthrottle`
- Repos/workspaces: `monorepo` (canonical `aec16344-9dee-477b-9430-9438b1f8dc8c`), `atlasworks`, `Atlasworks - Native Apps`

## Delete (48) — all `@openthrottle/*` + `@tools/*` package-projects
31 are clean (0 plans/0 tasks). 17 carry plan history — `delete_project` clears `project_id` on referenced plans/tasks (the plans/tasks survive, just unfiled), so we **reassign first, then delete** to preserve filing.

## Approach: reassign-then-delete
1. Task 1 — reassign the plans on the 17 attached package-projects to the mapped app/repo project (mapping in the task). nestjs-* → OpenThrottle Server; react-router-* + developer-codegen → OpenThrottle Developer; tools/agentic/workflows → monorepo.
2. Task 2 — delete all 48 package-projects by id.
3. Task 3 (optional) — remove the 2 empty duplicate `monorepo` projects.

Run mechanics: use the openthrottle-mcp tools — `update_plan {id, projectId}` (and `update_task {id, projectId}` if any tasks appear) to reassign, `delete_project {id}` to delete. Resolve current plan ids per source project at runtime via the `projects { id name plans { id } tasks { id } }` GraphQL query, since ids can drift before the run.
Delete the 48 OT projects that mirror individual workspace packages (@openthrottle/* and @tools/*). First reassign the 17 that carry plan history to the matching app/repo project, then delete all 48. Keep one project per application and per repo/workspace.

Token usage capture, persistence & Usage-route surfacing across agent-CLI drivers
## Goal

Turn per-turn token/cost usage — already parsed AND already normalized in the codebase, but only ephemerally on the client — into a **server-persisted, queryable, per-provider feed**, and surface it on the developer app's Usage route (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/usage._index.tsx`). v1: usage across all providers or narrowed to a single provider, with totals. Rich aggregations (rollups/trends/cost-over-time, budgets, non-chat sources) are an explicit longer-term follow-up carved into its own plan.

## Current state (what already exists — do NOT rebuild)

The heavy lifting is already done in three layers; the gap is a durable, aggregatable store + query + UI.

1. **Per-provider parsing already exists.** Each `ConversationBackend` in `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/<driver>/events.ts` maps its CLI's native structured output onto a terminal `usage`-kind `ConversationStreamChunk`. Shapes vary a lot (the "vary more than the APIs" the request calls out):
   - claude → `{ usage:{input_tokens,output_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens}, modelUsage, totalCostUsd, result }` (single terminal chunk)
   - grok → `{ usage, modelUsage, numTurns, stopReason }` (single terminal)
   - codex → `{ usage }` (single terminal `turn.completed`)
   - cursor → `{ usage }` (single terminal)
   - opencode → `{ cost, tokens:{total,input,output,reasoning,cache:{read,write}} }` emitted **mid-stream per `step_finish`** (`done:false`, MULTIPLE per turn → must be summed)
   - openai (HTTP backend) → its own usage shape
   Verified schema docs: `docs/openthrottle/{claude,grok,codex,cursor-agent}-stream-json-schema.md`.
2. **A canonical normalizer already exists — but only client-side.** `packages/react-router-chat/src/usage.ts` has `normalizeUsage()` (folds every heterogeneous backend shape into one `ChatTokenUsage`), `sumUsage()` (accumulates opencode's per-step counts), `hasUsageCounts`, `formatTokenCount`, `formatUsageCost`; `turn-events.ts#applyTurnUsage` folds a turn's usage into one event. `ChatTokenUsage` = `{ inputTokens?, outputTokens?, cacheReadTokens?, cacheWriteTokens?, totalTokens?, costUsd?, model? }` (`react-router-chat/src/types.ts`). **Reuse this as the canonical shape — do not invent a new one.** Caveat: `react-router-chat` is a browser package, so the normalizer must be lifted to a server-safe shared home (candidate: `openthrottle-agentic-utils` conversation-backend, co-located with the raw parsing and Node+browser-safe) and re-exported to `react-router-chat`, so the SAME normalization runs on the server persistence path. Reconciling these two parallel worlds is a design deliverable.
3. **Usage is already persisted — but unusably.** `ConversationStreamService.persistAssistant` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts`) collects usage chunks into `tool_metadata.events[]` JSONB on `agent_conversation_messages`. Per-message, heterogeneous, un-indexed, not aggregated, not queryable as totals.
4. **The Usage route has no token data.** `dailyStatsRange` / `DailyStatsObject` count only plans/tasks. Only `DashboardDailyStatsCard` (Recharts) and `UsageSnapshot` (JSON export) are data-bound; the rest is static copy. `UsageOverview`, `UsageDailyActivityOverview`, `UsageAnalyticsGaps` explicitly disclaim "No model token, cost, or latency metrics" — those become inaccurate once this ships and must be revised.

## The actual gap this plan fills

Server-side: (a) run the SAME normalizer on the persistence path, (b) write normalized usage to a durable, indexed, aggregatable store, (c) expose a user-scoped GraphQL query filterable by provider + date range returning per-turn/day rows + totals. Frontend: wire the Usage route to it and replace the disclaimers with a real per-provider usage surface.

## Related / overlapping work

- **Pending plan OT 32f38166** ("react-router-chat token usage plan — per-backend token/usage display; event model INERT"). That plan owns the *live in-chat display* of usage; THIS plan owns *durable server persistence + aggregation + the Usage analytics route*. Task 1 must draw the boundary and decide whether 32f38166's INERT event model should be activated as the client-side sibling, and whether the lifted normalizer supersedes part of it. Do not duplicate.

## Placement note

The variance lives in `openthrottle-agentic-utils` conversation-backend adapters (the streaming/parsing counterpart to `openthrottle-drivers`, which only builds CLI commands and today discards usage entirely). The canonical type + normalizers belong there / in a shared server-safe home — NOT in `openthrottle-drivers`. (Bringing usage into the plan-run/Ralph driver path, which uses plain-text output, is out of scope here.)

## Design decisions to lock in task 1

- Confirm `ChatTokenUsage` (+ any added fields e.g. `provider`, reasoningTokens) as the canonical persisted shape; where the shared server-safe normalizer lives; how `react-router-chat` re-consumes it.
- **Persistence model fork** (recommended: dedicated `agent_token_usage` fact table with nullable conversation/message/user FKs + indexes on (user_id, created_at), provider, model — decouples from chat so future sources (plan runs, Ralph) can write to it — over denormalized columns on `agent_conversation_messages`).
- Provider + model identity derivation per backend; usage cardinality (sum mid-stream opencode vs single terminal).
- GraphQL query shape (per-turn/day rows + totals object; filters provider?, start, end; user-scoped, authenticated).
- Boundary vs plan 32f38166; v1 scope vs deferred aggregations.

## Constraints / conventions

- Private mode (`persist=false`) must NOT write usage rows — turn is ephemeral.
- Code-first GraphQL (`autoSchemaFile` → `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`): after schema changes boot server, then `nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`; commit `schema.gql` + all `__generated__`. Deprecate, never break.
- SQL migration under `databases/migrations/` with COMMENT ON standards, idempotent DDL (ot-postgres skill).
- Follow Result/ListResult/PaginatedResult conventions.
- Frontend: `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` + `@tools/generators`; keep Recharts consistent with `DashboardDailyStatsCard`; components export only component+props, copy/data in nearest `data/` folder.

## Deferred (its own future plan)

Cross-provider rollups, trends, cost-over-time charts, budgets/alerts, and usage from non-chat sources (plan runs, Ralph iterations). Carve out once v1 capture+surfacing lands.

Skill usage tracking — harness-hook capture → OT persistence → Developer UI
## Goal

Observability into which agent skills actually get used, how often, in what context — across BOTH skills we author (skills/ → .agents/skills, tracked in skills-lock.json) and skills we do NOT control (vercel:*, engineering:*, anthropic-skills:*, etc.).

## Key design decision: instrument the harness, not the skill

Every skill — ours and third-party alike — is invoked through the **`Skill` tool**. So a **`PreToolUse` hook matching `Skill`** captures all of them with zero per-skill code, INCLUDING auto-triggered (description-match) invocations that a manual approach can never see.

**Rejected alternative:** a `/skill-tracking <name>` skill embedded in each of our skills. Rejected because it (a) only ever sees skills we author — the exact gap this plan must close, (b) misses auto-triggered invocations, (c) adds token overhead per skill, (d) is one forgotten edit from a blind spot. It survives only as optional depth-enrichment for our own skills (see final task), layered on top of the hook baseline, never as the primary mechanism.

Hooks are already proven in this repo — see the `WorktreeCreate` hook in `.claude/settings.json`.

## Data captured (decided)

Name + metadata + **truncated** args: `{ timestamp, skill_name, args (truncated/redacted), session_id, cwd, git_branch, scope: ours|third-party }`. Scope is derived by looking the skill name up against `skills-lock.json` / `skills/`.

The privacy level (name-only → truncated → full args) is deliberately abstracted so it can become a configurable knob — tracked as a SEPARATE OT plan (future/paid-feature track). This plan ships with truncated-args as the fixed default.

## Open unknowns the spike MUST settle (do not assume)

1. **Subagent coverage** — do `PreToolUse` hooks fire for `Skill` calls made INSIDE subagents (Ralph / Workflow fan-out)? If not, that's a real coverage gap to name loudly.
2. **Privacy/retention** — confirm truncation/redaction rules and a retention window before args ever hit Postgres.
3. **Sink of record** — local JSONL as fallback; OT server as system of record.

## Phased delivery

- Phase 0: Spike — prove the mechanism + payload, settle unknowns.
- Phase 1: Local JSONL capture hook (MVP, zero infra).
- Phase 2: OT server table + ingest mutation; hook posts fail-open (falls back to JSONL).
- Phase 3: Surface in Developer UI (Skills / Usage route), mirroring the token-usage capture pattern (commit e51ebb8e, Usage route, OT a55b76ba).

## Prior art to mirror

Token usage capture/persistence/surfacing (commit e51ebb8e; OT plan a55b76ba) and the existing Skills detail route (OT 6c785a74) are the closest patterns — same server→codegen→UI shape.
Track every skill invocation (ours AND third-party) via a PreToolUse hook on the Skill tool, persist to OT Postgres, and surface usage in the Developer UI. Hook-based, not per-skill instrumentation.

Chat turn idle-timeout backstop + auto-retry recovery for hangers
## Problem

Every so often a chat turn "hangs": the backend stalls, no further deltas arrive, and no terminal `done` chunk is ever published. The server's `runStream()` `for await` loop blocks indefinitely, so the turn never persists and never emits a terminal chunk; the client stays `isStreaming: true` forever (`pendingAssistantId` never clears) and the composer is stuck. Today the only exit is the manual Stop button, and there is **no retry** anywhere in the chat UI. These hangs are the kind we could simply have interrupted and recovered from with a retry.

## Locked decisions
- **Timeout posture: idle-only.** Fire only when no chunk has arrived for N seconds — safe for legitimately long CLI agent runs that keep emitting output; catches true stalls. No aggressive wall-clock cap on the orchestrator (CLI backends keep their own wall-clock as a last resort).
- **Recovery: auto-retry once, then manual.** On a retryable timeout, silently re-run the turn once; if it stalls again, surface the error + a manual Retry button.

## Current architecture (verified)

Streaming spine: `submitTurn()` → `intent=start` POST to `/resources/conversation-stream` → `startConversationStream` mutation → `ConversationStreamService.start()` → fire-and-forget `runStream()` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts:211`) → `for await (const chunk of backend.stream(backendRun))` → `publishChunk()` → in-process PubSub topic `conversation:<id>:stream` → `conversationStreamChunkAdded` subscription → `useConversationStream` hook (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/useConversationStream.tsx`) → `reduceStreamChunk` (`packages/react-router-chat/src/conversation-stream.ts`) → `useAgenticChatTurn` (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/useAgenticChatTurn.tsx`). Chunk shape `{ id, conversationId, messageId, delta, done, error, kind, metadataJson, sortOrder }`.

Existing timeout/abort inventory:
- Per-conversation `AbortController` + `cancel()` **exist** in the service (line 115/177), driven today only by the user's Stop button — no timer.
- **CLI backends already self-terminate**: claude/codex/grok/cursor-agent/opencode wrap their subprocess in idle + wall-clock timeouts via `resolveAgentTimeouts()` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/cursor-agent/teardown.ts`; `idleMs` default 120_000 env `OPENTHROTTLE_AGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `wallClockMs` 900_000, `graceMs` 5_000) + SIGTERM→SIGKILL teardown.
- **Gap 1 — HTTP/OpenAI backend is unbounded**: `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/openai.ts` → `chat-completions/stream.ts` only forwards `options.signal`; a mid-stream silent endpoint hangs the iterator.
- **Gap 2 — no orchestrator backstop**: `runStream()` trusts each backend to terminate; any wedged backend hangs the turn with no terminal chunk.
- **Gap 3 — no retry**: grep for `watchdog|stall|retry|setInterval` across the chat hooks + `react-router-chat/src` returns nothing. `StreamState` carries no last-activity timestamp for a client watchdog.

Surfaces sharing the path: the global header chat wraps `useAgenticChatTurn` via `useHeaderChatController`; the admin app has its own copy under `applications/openthrottle-admin/app/routes/resources.conversation-stream.tsx`. A separate, lower-priority legacy single-shot path (`packages/react-router-chat/src/hooks/useChatTurnFetcher.tsx`, `intent=send-agent-message`) also has no timeout. Reference pattern for timeout+abort+kill already implemented for the (unrelated) Ralph driver path in `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/engine/index.ts` (`runDriverAsync`).

## Approach

1. **Server orchestrator idle-timeout backstop** in `runStream()` — the single choke point covering ALL backends including the unbounded HTTP one. Race the backend iterator against an idle timer (reset on each chunk); on expiry call the existing `controller.abort()` AND break the loop so a backend that ignores its signal still terminates. Persist whatever streamed, then publish a terminal `done` chunk carrying a clear timeout message + a machine-readable retryable marker.
2. **HTTP/OpenAI backend idle timeout** to match the CLI backends' `resetIdle()` behavior, using the shared `resolveAgentTimeouts()`.
3. **Retryable terminal-chunk contract** propagated through the shared reducer/types so the client can distinguish "timed out — retry" from a fatal error.
4. **Client auto-retry-once + watchdog** in `useAgenticChatTurn`: remember the last `(message, fields)`, track last activity, auto-resubmit once on a retryable terminal chunk (or a client-side stall if the subscription dies), guarded against loops; expose a manual Retry after.
5. **Manual Retry UI affordance** + **header/admin parity** + **tests** + **config/docs/validation**.

Reuse the existing `resolveAgentTimeouts()` env knobs (or add a chat-scoped alias) for consistency; keep defaults conservative so healthy long CLI runs are unaffected.
Add a high-level idle timeout to the streaming chat turn so a hung backend always terminates and publishes a terminal error chunk, then auto-retry the turn once (manual Retry after) so users recover from stalls without a stuck composer.

Rollout v1: feature-flagging system (@openthrottle/nestjs-rollout + /settings/rollout UI)
## What

Introduce **"rollout"** — OpenThrottle's feature-flagging system — as a new `@openthrottle/nestjs-rollout` package plus an admin CRUD UI at `/settings/rollout` in `openthrottle-developer`. It integrates with `@openthrottle/nestjs-rbac` from day one.

> Terminology: **rollout** = the feature-flagging system (this plan). **clutch** = the Agentic Chat & harness (a *separate* system, unrelated to this plan — noted only to avoid naming collisions).

## v1 scope (locked)

- **Flag model — global + role targeting.** A flag = `key` (unique, kebab/dotted string), `description`, `enabled` (bool), `targetRoles` (string[] of RBAC role names). Evaluation: a flag is ON for an actor when `enabled === true` AND (`targetRoles` is empty ⇒ everyone, else the actor holds ≥1 of `targetRoles`).
- **Consumption — server service + GraphQL query.** `RolloutService.isEnabled(key, principal)` for server-side code, plus a `myFeatureFlags` GraphQL query returning the evaluated flag set for the current actor.
- **RBAC integration.** New `flags:read` / `flags:write` permissions added to `@openthrottle/nestjs-rbac`. Admin mutations are gated by the app's `GqlPermissionsGuard` + `@Permissions(...)`. Role targeting resolves the actor's roles via `RolesService` (from `@openthrottle/nestjs-repositories`), exactly as `GqlPermissionsGuard` does.

Out of scope for v1 (candidate v2): percentage/bucketed rollout, per-user overrides, environment/segment targeting, audit history, SDK/edge caching.

## Architecture boundary (mirrors the existing roles precedent)

The **package owns the domain**: the TypeORM entity, `RolloutFlagsModule` (`TypeOrmModule.forFeature`), and `RolloutService` (CRUD + evaluation; depends on `@openthrottle/nestjs-repositories` `RolesService` and `@openthrottle/nestjs-auth` `AuthPrincipal`). The **GraphQL resolver lives in the app** (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/rollout/`) because it must use the app-local `GqlPermissionsGuard` (the app depends on packages, not the reverse). This is precisely how `RolesService` (in `nestjs-repositories`) pairs with `RolesResolver` (in the app).

## Conventions confirmed by research (apply throughout)

- **Package**: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:package --type=nestjs --organization=@openthrottle --name=nestjs-rollout`. # Generic scheduled agent jobs

## Why
Every recurring agent job today requires a bespoke, code-defined queue + processor + `*-repeatable.service.ts` (there are 5 cron services). There is **no way for a user to create a scheduled agent job at runtime**: no persistence, no create-repeatable mutation (only `repeatableJobs` list + `removeRepeatableJob`), and the only agent worker (`PlansProcessor`) is hardwired to the Ralph orchestrator + a single Cursor iteration runner.

We want a **generic** scheduled job: give it a **prompt + provider/model/settings**, pick a **cron schedule**, and it runs on BullMQ's built-in repeatable machinery — one shared queue, no new queue per job — usable with any agent framework/CLI.

## Approach (locked)
- **Runner primitive lives in `openthrottle-drivers`** — that's our choke point and most of it already exists (`ALL_DRIVERS`/`getDriver`, `AgentDriver.buildShellCommand`, `DriverInvocationConfig`, `runDriverAsync`/`runDriverSync` engine across claude/codex/cursor/grok/opencode). The design must **inventory what already exists there first** and extend/expose a single provider-agnostic "run once with {prompt, driverId, model, settings, cwd, signal, onChunk}" entrypoint rather than reinventing invocation in the server.
- **Server adds ONE generic queue + processor** (modeled on `PlansProcessor`: heartbeat, AbortSignal cancellation, output logging, stalled recovery) that decodes `{scheduleId, prompt, driverId, model, settings}` and calls the drivers entrypoint. Decoupled from Ralph/plans.
- **BullMQ repeatable jobs** provide the scheduling (reuse `REPEATABLE_JOB_OPTIONS`; evaluate legacy `repeat` vs newer `upsertJobScheduler`). No dedicated queue per user job.

## Net-new
- Persistence for user-defined schedules (no table exists today).
- A create/update/delete/enable/run-now GraphQL surface (only list/remove repeatables exist).
- Reconciliation between persisted schedules and BullMQ schedulers.
- A generic driver-invocation worker (current one is Ralph/Cursor-specific).
- Developer UI to author schedules (prompt + provider/model/settings + cron) and view run history/live logs.

## Design-first
Task 1 is an architecture design doc (under `docs/`) that must resolve: the drivers-package entrypoint API, the generic queue payload + naming, persistence schema (schedule + runs), legacy `repeat` vs `upsertJobScheduler`, DB↔BullMQ reconciliation, where run output/logs live (reuse `queueJobLogs`/work-ledger?), role-slicing, and the GraphQL contract. Implementation tasks follow the doc.

## Key anchor files
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/{types,drivers,registry,engine}/index.ts`
- `packages/nestjs-bullmq/src/modules/nestjs-bullmq.module.ts`, `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/repeatable-job.options.ts`
- Reference services: `.../queues/doc-ingestion/doc-ingestion-repeatable.service.ts` (env-driven cron), `.../queues/work-ledger-sweep/work-ledger-sweep-repeatable.service.ts`
- Reference worker: `.../queues/plans/plans.processor.ts`; enqueue path `.../graphql/plans/plan-enqueue.service.ts`
- Dynamic-queue caveat: `.../graphql/queues/queues.service.ts` `createQueue` makes a producer-only queue (no processor) — a generic job needs a statically-registered processor.
Design-first feature: let users create scheduled agent jobs from a prompt + provider/model/settings that run on a cron schedule via BullMQ's built-in repeatable jobs, WITHOUT a dedicated queue per job. The provider-agnostic run-once primitive stays in openthrottle-drivers (the choke point — runDriverAsync/engine already exists); the server adds one generic queue + processor, persistence, reconciliation, GraphQL, and a developer UI.

Harden SSR against deferred-loader rejections (never crash) + fix the auth-error contract — all RR apps
## Problem

Loading a protected page with an **expired session** (or any authed GraphQL failure inside a deferred loader) **crashes the React Router SSR dev/prod server**. Observed as `Error: GraphQL errors: Unauthorized` thrown from `callListAgentConversations` (the dashboard "Recent Chats" card) with no React Router frames in the stack — i.e. an **unhandled promise rejection**, which Node crashes on by default (`--unhandled-rejections=throw`).

This is one instance of a **class** of bug: any authenticated GraphQL call returned from a loader as a **naked deferred promise** (RR8 Single Fetch streaming) that rejects, with no synchronous `.catch` attached before the microtask, takes down the whole SSR process. `<Await errorElement>` does **not** prevent it — errorElement runs at render time, too late to stop the unhandled rejection.

## Root causes (two, compounding)

1. **The auth-error contract is dead code.** `@openthrottle/react-router-graphql` already ships typed `GraphqlAuthError` (with `httpStatus`), `isAuthError`, `GraphqlTimeoutError`, `isTimeoutError`, and `classifyError()` (`extractHttpStatus` on the error message). But the NestJS GraphQL guard returns **HTTP 200 with a GraphQL error `"Unauthorized"` / `extensions.code: UNAUTHENTICATED`** — there is no HTTP status in the message, so `classifyError` never recognizes it. Auth-detection never fires (confirmed by the `/improve` audit for this package, plan `6d479fa3`). So even the code meant to make auth failures redirectable is inert.
2. **Deferral relied on `<Await errorElement>`** to handle rejections (the plan that introduced dashboard/home deferral, `f9030c40`, says so explicitly) — which cannot stop a microtask-level unhandled rejection.

## Already shipped (L0 — prevention)

`authMiddleware` now treats a **present-but-expired** JWT like a missing one: `isJwtExpired()` pre-flight → clear cookie + redirect to `/auth`. This prevents the **common** case (stale session) from ever reaching loaders. Landed on branch `openthrottle/loop-plan-mcp-connectors`, commit `4ced2b1f` (`packages/react-router-auth`: `isJwtExpired` + middleware gate + tests). This plan covers the remaining, non-expiry cases and the crash-class itself.

## Decision (locked with the owner)

**Defense-in-depth (L1 + L2 + L3), scoped as shared packages so all four RR apps inherit it once.**

- **L1 — Safety net (never crash):** a shared process-level `unhandledRejection` (and `uncaughtException`) handler that **logs, does not exit**. A backstop, not the fix — a logged error is strictly better than a dead server. One shared helper, wired into every app's `app/entry.server.tsx`.
- **L2 — Fix the auth-error contract (auth failures become clean redirects):** extend `classifyError` (or the underlying `@openthrottle/nodejs-graphql` error contract) so a GraphQL `UNAUTHENTICATED` / `"Unauthorized"` error IS classified as `GraphqlAuthError`; plus a single shared `redirectOnAuthError` loader/action helper (redirect to `/auth` + clear cookie) replacing the ~6 hand-rolled per-route auth redirects. Overlaps the existing improve plans `6d479fa3` (react-router-graphql) and `798d5efc` (react-router-auth — single owner of a typed `isUnauthorizedError`) — fold/reference rather than duplicate.
- **L3 — Resilient deferred helper (root-cause fix):** a shared helper for deferred loader values that attaches its `.catch` **synchronously** so the promise can never go unhandled: auth errors → `throw redirect('/auth')` (RR honors thrown redirects even in streamed data); other errors → a resolved error-state value the card renders (or a synchronously-caught re-throw the `<Await errorElement>` handles). Open design point resolved in task 1: **opt-in helper (adoption discipline) vs. an automatic entry-level wrapper that walks loader return values (can't-forget).**

## Scope

All four React Router apps — `openthrottle-developer`, `openthrottle-admin`, `openthrottle-email`, `openthrottle-website` — each with its own `app/entry.server.tsx` (renderToPipeableStream). Shared code lands in `@openthrottle/react-router-utils` (server-entry safety net + deferred helper) and `@openthrottle/react-router-graphql` / `@openthrottle/react-router-auth` (auth-error contract + redirect helper), so apps inherit the behavior rather than re-implement it.

## Grounding facts (confirmed)

- `react-router-graphql` exports: `GraphqlAuthError`, `isAuthError`, `GraphqlTimeoutError`, `isTimeoutError`, `classifyError`, `extractHttpStatus` (`packages/react-router-graphql/src/index.ts`).
- The failing rejection surfaces as `Error: "GraphQL errors: Unauthorized"` (from `@openthrottle/nodejs-graphql` `index.ts:123`), i.e. HTTP 200 + `errors[0].message = "Unauthorized"`, `extensions.code = UNAUTHENTICATED` — **no HTTP status**, so `extractHttpStatus` returns undefined and it is NOT classified as auth.
- `@openthrottle/nodejs-graphql` already has a non-throwing v2 discriminated-union contract (`executeGraphql_v2`, `GraphqlV2Result`, `httpStatus`) that L2 can adopt instead of string-scraping (see `6d479fa3` roadmap).
- Deferred loaders in play today: `dashboard._index.tsx` (`core` / `githubStats` / `recentChats`) and home `_index.tsx` (composer bundle) — from plan `f9030c40`.

## Verification (per the touched apps)

- Reproduce all three failure modes against a running dev server and assert **no process crash**: (a) expired token, (b) mid-session 401/`UNAUTHENTICATED` on a deferred call, (c) API down / timeout on a deferred call. Expected: auth → 302 `/auth` (+ cleared cookie); non-auth → the card/section shows a degraded error state; the server stays up.
- Gates on every touched project: `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`; no GraphQL schema/codegen drift (no server schema change expected).

## Related plans

- `6d479fa3` — Improve: @openthrottle/react-router-graphql (auth-error contract, `redirectOnAuthError`).
- `798d5efc` — Improve: @openthrottle/react-router-auth (single owner of a typed auth-error helper).
- `f9030c40` — Defer slow loader data on Developer home + dashboard (introduced the naked-promise pattern).

Each task carries its own acceptance criteria in `requirements`. Commit per task with `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers.
A deferred (streamed) loader promise that rejects with no synchronous catch becomes an unhandled rejection and crashes the RR SSR process (Node --unhandled-rejections=throw). Fix it once, globally, via defense-in-depth across all 4 React Router apps: L1 a shared process-level unhandledRejection safety net (log, never exit), L2 fix the broken auth-error contract so GraphQL UNAUTHENTICATED errors are classified + a shared redirectOnAuthError helper, L3 a resilient deferred-value helper so deferred loader promises can never go unhandled (auth → thrown redirect, other → resolved error-state). L0 (expired-token redirect in authMiddleware) already shipped.

Model discovery caching: faster repeat loads
## Problem

Agent-CLI and local-model discovery feel slow on repeat loads. Investigation of the current caching found that the ONLY real cache is two 60s in-process singleton caches on the server; the client re-fetches on every mount/navigation, and the home loader amplifies each load into 2x calls per query. Every ~60s the next request pays the full cold cost (spawning up to 5 `--version` + 3 `<cli> models` child processes with 3s/5s timeouts, plus ~48 HTTP probes for local models).

## Current caching (as-is)

- **Local models** — `NestjsModelDiscoveryService` (`packages/nestjs-model-discovery/src/nestjs-model-discovery.service.ts`): singleton, 60s TTL (`LLM_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS`, default 60_000), has both cache + `inFlight` promise coalescing + `invalidate()`. Good citizen.
- **Agent CLIs** — `AgentDiscoveryService` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-discovery/agent-discovery.service.ts`): singleton, `CACHE_TTL_MS = 60_000`, cache-only. **NO in-flight dedup** — concurrent cache-miss callers each launch a full CLI sweep.
- **Client** — none. `executeGraphqlWithAuth` is plain fetch; no React Query/Apollo/localStorage/Jotai memoization. No HTTP cache headers on resolvers.

## Repeat-load amplifiers

- Home route loader `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx` fires all three discovery loaders every load; `loadDriverEndpointModels` (`models.server.ts`) re-issues BOTH GraphQL queries, so one home load triggers `discoverLocalModels` x2 and `discoverAgentClis` x2 (deduped only by the 60s server TTL, not the client).
- Header chat `useHeaderChatController.tsx` calls `optionsFetcher.load('/resources/chat-options')` per mount; a page reload re-fetches. `routes/resources.chat-options.tsx` re-runs both discovery loaders.
- Both loaders swallow errors -> `[]`, so failures silently re-probe next time.
- Multi-instance/serverless server deployments each keep their own in-memory cache -> low hit rate.

## GraphQL surface

- `discoverLocalModels` -> `ModelDiscoveryResolver` -> `NestjsModelDiscoveryService`
- `discoverAgentClis` -> `AgentDiscoveryResolver` -> `AgentDiscoveryService`
- Both guarded by `@Permissions(SETTINGS_READ)`. MCP tools go through the same cached queries.

## Levers to evaluate/apply

1. In-flight coalescing on `AgentDiscoveryService` (parity with model-discovery).
2. Stale-while-revalidate / background refresh: serve last-good snapshot instantly, refresh out of band, so repeat loads never pay cold cost.
3. Dedupe the double-fetch in `_index.tsx` / `loadDriverEndpointModels`.
4. Client-side caching so repeat mounts/navigations don't re-hit the server (persist loader result + `shouldRevalidate`, and/or HTTP cache headers on the resolvers).
5. Optional: shared cache (Redis) for multi-instance deployments — evaluate cost/benefit vs longer TTL.

## Approach

Design-first: task 1 measures current repeat-load cost and locks the chosen levers before code changes. Keep changes behind the existing config knobs where possible. Validate repeat-load latency drops and add regression tests.
Speed up agent-CLI + local-model discovery on repeat loads: add in-flight coalescing + stale-while-revalidate to the server caches, dedupe the home-loader double-fetch, and add client-side caching so repeat mounts/navigations don't re-probe.

# Defer slow loader data on Developer home + dashboard

## Problem

Navigating into `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx` (home composer) and `dashboard._index.tsx` feels sluggish because each route **blocks its entire render** on slow GraphQL work in the loader. React Router waits for the loader to fully resolve before it will transition, so the shell (heading, sidebar, nav chrome) is held hostage by data that only a sub-tree needs.

Two concrete offenders:

- **`_index.tsx`** — the loader does `Promise.all` of **five** discovery queries (`loadDiscoveredModels`, `loadAgentClis`, `loadDriverEndpointModels`, `loadRepositories`, `loadPersonas`). `loadDiscoveredModels` / `loadDriverEndpointModels` probe locally-running model servers (Ollama, etc.); cold, that is the slow path. Nothing paints — not the "What would you like to build today?" hero, not the conversation sidebar, not a disabled composer — until all five settle. Only the toolbar (`reconcileChatToolbarState`, `buildModelGroups`) actually needs `models`/`personas`/`repositories`.
- **`dashboard._index.tsx`** — worse: the loader `await`s `GetDashboardDocument` and **then sequentially** `await`s `GetDashboardGithubStatsDocument` (a GitHub API round-trip). Two serial network calls block the intro banner and the "This Week's Activity" chart, neither of which depends on GitHub stats.

## Approach — deferred (streamed) loader data

Move the slow work off the critical render path so the **shell paints instantly** and slow data **streams in** behind Suspense fallbacks.

**Idiom (important):** this app is on **react-router 8.0.1**, where the `defer()` helper has been removed. The modern equivalent is to **return naked promises** from the loader (Single Fetch serializes/streams them) and consume them in the component with `React.Suspense` + `<Await resolve={promise} errorElement={…}>` + `useAsyncValue()`. Streaming SSR is already in place — `entry.server.tsx` uses `renderToPipeableStream`, so deferred promises flush progressively. No `future` flags or `defer()` import needed.

### Per-route strategy

**Home (`_index.tsx`)**
- Keep the loader signature returning an object, but return the composer-data bundle as a **promise** instead of awaited values. The hero heading and the conversation sidebar (`useConversationList` is a client hook — already independent of the loader) render immediately.
- The composer/toolbar sub-tree — everything that consumes `models` / `personas` / `repositories` via `reconcileChatToolbarState`, `buildModelGroups`, and `capabilitiesForChatOption` — moves under `<Suspense fallback={<composer skeleton, disabled>}><Await>`. Because reconciliation needs all three lists together, bundle them into one awaited `Promise.all` promise (not three independent awaits) so the toolbar reconciles atomically.
- Fallback: a disabled composer skeleton reading e.g. "Discovering models…" so the input frame is visibly present instantly.

**Dashboard (`dashboard._index.tsx`)**
- First, stop the serial waterfall: fire `GetDashboard` and `GetDashboardGithubStats` **concurrently**.
- Return two independent deferred promises so the "This Week's Activity" chart streams as soon as the dashboard query lands, without waiting on the slower GitHub call. GitHub-dependent cards (PR time-in-state, PRs by author) get their own `<Suspense>` boundary with skeletons.
- The intro banner + grid scaffold render synchronously.
- **Error handling:** `dashboard._index` calls `executeGraphqlWithAuth` **without** a try/catch, so a deferred promise can reject. Each `<Await>` must supply an `errorElement` (inline per-section error) so a GitHub-stats failure degrades that card instead of throwing the whole route to the ErrorBoundary. (The home helpers already catch → `[]`, so those promises resolve rather than reject — but still guard defensively.)

## Skeletons / fallbacks
Use `Skeleton` from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`. New skeleton components follow repo conventions: one component per file under the route's `components/` folder, section comments, component-only exports (copy/data in a sibling `data/` folder if any). Inventory: composer-loading skeleton (home), dashboard activity-chart skeleton, dashboard PR-cards skeleton.

## Gotchas to watch
- `Route.ComponentProps['loaderData']` will now carry `Promise<…>` fields; `HandleData` (used by the breadcrumb `handle`) becomes promise-shaped — the breadcrumb returns a literal string so it still typechecks, but confirm.
- Existing route tests (`app/routes/__tests__/dashboard._index.test.tsx`, home `_index` tests) assert on resolved content and mock loaders returning plain objects. With deferral they must switch to async `findBy*` queries and add fallback-state assertions. Keep the repo test conventions (`component` not `screen`, `userEvent`).
- Don't over-defer: the shell + anything cheap stays synchronous. Only the genuinely slow discovery/GitHub work is deferred.

## Out of scope (note as follow-up)
The **root loader** (`root.tsx`) also runs on every navigation (health probe + `me` query, already concurrent) and contributes baseline transition latency. Not part of this plan — flag as a possible follow-up if transitions still feel slow after these two routes are deferred.

## Verification
- Dev server, navigate home ↔ dashboard ↔ home: shell must paint immediately, with skeletons visibly streaming into real content. Verify via the in-app browser preview tools (console/network clean, screenshot the streamed state).
- Gates: `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` on `openthrottle-developer` (plus codegen unaffected — no GraphQL schema change).

Explore & ship a curated MCP **connectors** catalog with a connect flow, surfaced under `/settings/mcp` in `openthrottle-developer`.

## Context / gap
OpenThrottle today exposes *its own* tools **as** an MCP server (`packages/openthrottle-mcp`, `applications/openthrottle-server/src/modules/mcp-developer`). It has **no** concept of the platform *connecting to external* MCP servers (GitHub, Slack, Notion…) that agents could later consume. This plan adds the first vertical slice: a curated catalog + connect/enable flow.

## Locked decisions (2026-07-31)
- **Baseline** = curated **top ~10** connectors seeded across **3 registry/host providers**: (1) Anthropic connector directory, (2) the official MCP registry, (3) vendor-hosted remote MCP. Live registry tools returned nothing in-session, so Task 1 curates from known connectors rather than a live pull.
- **Scope** = **catalog + connect flow**: browse → connect (store credential / OAuth reference, mirroring `settings.keys`) → enable/disable. **No agent-run wiring** in this plan (explicit follow-up).
- **Route** = **`/settings/mcp`** (`settings.mcp._index.tsx` + `settings.mcp.$connectorId.tsx`).

## Proposed top-10 (finalized in Task 1)
GitHub, Linear, Notion, Slack, Atlassian (Jira/Confluence), Sentry, Google Drive, Figma, Stripe, Postgres/Supabase — each tagged with its source provider + auth type (OAuth vs token) + remote transport config.

## Key patterns to follow
- Flat routes (`settings.mcp.*.tsx`) + companion `.graphql` docs + `__tests__`; logic/components under `app/routing/settings/`.
- Credential storage mirrors the service-account-credential flow in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.keys.tsx` and its server resolvers.
- Code-first GraphQL in `openthrottle-server` (Result/ListResult types; never break fields, `@deprecated`); regenerate `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` + codegen.
- Generators first (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=...`), one component/file, keep section comments, no TS enums (`as const`).
- Authed pages need permissions → prefer render-level Vitest (repo memory: developer-app-live-verify-auth-permission).

## Out of scope (future plans)
Wiring enabled connectors into live agent runs / drivers; per-connector tool allow-lists; org-vs-user connection scoping beyond the baseline.
